item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model rated "Critical" on its Preparedness Framework
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to vetted defenders, claiming better exploit-finding and far fewer out-of-scope actions, and its Preparedness Framework rates it "Critical" for cybersecurity. (The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Anthropic lets Claude read your bank accounts with a new Personal Finance feature
item.description: Anthropic launched a beta Personal Finance tool that links Claude to bank and card accounts through Plaid with read-only access, following a similar ChatGPT feature from May. (The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: ToolSpace builds agent training tasks from how real tools are chained in execution traces, producing cross-service workflows that lift open models toward frontier tool-use scores. (Guanting Dong, Zhichao Sun, Xinyu Yang et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
item.description: Merging several specialist models into one with on-policy distillation reaches near-teacher scores on training tasks yet loses ground on harder or combined tasks, unless supervision is also broadened. (Yichen Wang, Yufa Zhou, Siqi Zhu et al. · University of Chicago, Duke University, UIUC)

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
item.description: Fine-tuning a generalist robot policy with value-based reinforcement learning across many tasks improves it on unseen objects and scenes, which single-task fine-tuning does not. (Michal Korniak, Marco Bagatella, Ralf Römer et al. · ETH Zurich, MPI for Intelligent Systems, Technical University of Munich)

item.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
item.description: PEARL trains a language model to recover from partly misaligned starts, making removal of a bad behavior far more resistant to later fine-tuning than standard supervised or reinforcement learning fixes. (Luxi He, Pengcheng Jiang, Jifan Zhang et al. · Princeton University, UIUC, Thinking Machines Lab)

item.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
item.description: Speculative decoding is lossless in distribution but not in numerical precision, and the authors train the draft model to disagree at key decision points to improve long-horizon coding agents. (Hongyin Luo, Wei Fang, Lijie Yang et al. · Subconscious)

item.title: Midterm results make the data-center backlash a political force that could slow AI buildout
item.description: US voters backed candidates and ballot measures that restrict data centers, and with Democrats winning Congress, new limits on the buildout behind AI are now more likely. (The Verge, TechCrunch, Wired)

item.title: Moonshot AI releases the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3T-class agentic model
item.description: Moonshot AI published open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, a natively multimodal agentic model with a one-million-token context window, post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale reinforcement learning. (Moonshot AI (Hugging Face model card))

item.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
item.description: IdeaTaste scores LLM-written research proposals against what a field actually published later, finding models match only about 18% of the human level on ideas. (Shanshan Zhong, Chen Xu, Jingjie Ning et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence)

item.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
item.description: NEO-VLA drops the separate vision encoder from a robot policy and lets its action module read visual features from many backbone layers, beating encoder-based baselines on LIBERO. (Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu et al. · MMLab@NTU)

item.title: You don't need long context
item.description: NVIDIA researchers show frontier models keep most of their accuracy on long-horizon and long-input tasks when forced to work in short contexts through frequent compaction. (Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
item.description: FrontierPhysics has 42 physicists turn their own research into 56 end-to-end tasks, and no AI agent configuration passes more than 46 of 168 attempts. (Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer et al. · Multi-institution team of physicists (26 institutions))

item.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
item.description: SpecOPD trains speculative-decoding draft models on their own sampled outputs in parallel branches, lifting accepted-token length by up to 41% and training throughput 16x. (Tianyu Liu, Jun Zhang, Wenjie Huang et al. · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba, University of Science and Technology of China, Zhejiang University)

item.title: Google will switch off Search for schools that reject its AI tools
item.description: Google will turn its AI tools off by default for K-12 student accounts, but schools that keep them off also lose Google Search, because Google treats Search and AI as one product. (TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica)

item.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
item.description: An open-weight Qwen model, driven through a carefully designed tool harness and with no privileged inputs, beats the published GPT-6 Astra result on the RoboDojo robot benchmark. (Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang et al. · Tsinghua University, UC Berkeley)

item.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
item.description: A 240-task benchmark scores AI agents as teammates and finds that even the best model reaches only 82.2 out of 100, with strong models caving under social pressure and keeping inherited cheating. (Sean Wu, Aneesh Pappu, Jiaru Zou et al. · Stanford University, University of Oxford, MIT)

item.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
item.description: Muon beats AdamW at pretraining loss but, with enough pretraining data, AdamW models fine-tune better, and the crossover arrives sooner as models grow. (Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski et al.)

item.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
item.description: DR Pixel does deep research directly on rendered page images instead of OCR text, and a step-weighted fine-tuning method lifts a 27B open model to GPT-5.4-level accuracy. (Tiansheng Hu, Yichuan Wang, James V. Talwar et al. · NYU Shanghai, UC Berkeley, Rational Dynamics)

item.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Turning a judge's per-turn text feedback into a self-distillation signal, only on failing turns and alongside normal RL rewards, teaches coding agents behaviors that plain RL never discovers. (Kevin Frans, Alexander M Rush, Sergey Levine et al. · Cursor Research, UC Berkeley)

item.title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says it may imminently reach its own "dramatically accelerated progress" threshold
item.description: In a revised S-1/A filed Monday, Anthropic wrote that its internal estimates suggest it may imminently meet the Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of AI-driven dramatically accelerated progress, while saying no current model crosses it. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Researchers show GPT-6 Astra can read and directly edit neural network weights, lifting a small Qwen model's math score
item.description: A blog post reports that GPT-6 Astra, without writing training loops, identified a flaw in Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and fixed it by editing 0.016% of them, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. (Weight-Space Programming blog post)

item.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
item.description: Giving models partial reference solutions turns a hard benchmark into a smooth family of easier ones, letting scaling laws fit on small, near-zero-accuracy models forecast large-model benchmark accuracy with far lower error. (Suze van Adrichem, Luke Bailey, Rohith Kuditipudi et al. · Stanford University)

item.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
item.description: Wave Forcing lets several video chunks denoise at once on different GPUs, with earlier chunks serving as cleaner context for later ones, reaching about 135 end-to-end frames per second on eight H200 GPUs. (Yijie Jin, Yuxuan Liu, Jiajun Xu et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Peking University)

item.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
item.description: In a video-plus-action world model, videos of new tasks without action labels lift out-of-distribution success on RoboTwin 2.0 from 25% to 56%, and one labeled demonstration per task lifts it to 71%. (Jun Cen, Yubo Guo, Hao Li et al. · Joy Future Academy)

item.title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
item.description: Jet-QSparse stores the KV cache in 4-bit NVFP4 and aggregates values from selected blocks only, giving 1.94 times faster decoding and 2.58 to 2.76 times cache capacity without training. (Haozhan Tang, Hao Kang, Meng Lu et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Virginia Tech, Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

item.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
item.description: CoworkOS is an open agent harness that separates strategy from execution management, matches or beats Codex-style harnesses on 12 benchmarks, and drives five rounds of automated post-training that lifted a Qwen model by 9.76 points. (Jiajie Jin, Guanting Dong, Chengjun Pan et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Peking University)

item.title: Marvell agrees to buy optical-chip maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal
item.description: Marvell will acquire laser and optical-module maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, a bet that AI data centers are moving from copper to integrated optical connectivity. (Marvell Investor Relations)

item.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
item.description: LARC lets a unified image model think in continuous hidden states instead of text before drawing, trained with a curriculum and a self-supervised information-gain reward, and it improves with more thinking. (Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al. · KAIST, POSTECH, RLWRLD)

item.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
item.description: ID-WM plans long tasks by using diffusion noise as an abstract action that picks reachable subgoals, while a second model converts each hop into precise actions. (Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al. · New York University (Courant Institute), Meta FAIR, AMI Labs)

item.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
item.description: CaPtain turns a 4B open vision-language model, which initially solves nothing, into a robot agent that writes code against low-level primitives, using synthetic supervision and reinforcement learning with a simulator-informed critic. (Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang et al. · Chinese University of Hong Kong (MMLab), NovaXBot)

item.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
item.description: Chronos-2 is a 120M-parameter zero-shot forecaster that uses group attention to learn relationships among related series and covariates in context, trained only on synthetic multivariate data. (Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken et al. · Amazon Web Services, University of Freiburg, Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry)

item.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
item.description: ACCT converts a small model's already-computed context cache into a compressed cache that a larger model in the same family can use directly, skipping the large model's expensive prefill. (Yuzhe Liu, Haolin Tian, Tonghan Wang · Tsinghua University)

item.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its new funding round's target to $20 billion as investors cool
item.description: The Financial Times reports OpenAI lowered its new round's target from $30 billion to $20 billion, and the Wall Street Journal says $11 billion is secured, during a tech-stock selloff over AI spending. (TechCrunch, The Next Web)

item.title: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite answers its first prompt, running Gemma 4 on a TPU in orbit
item.description: Google's first Project Suncatcher prototype, carrying four TPUs, answered a prompt from orbit with Gemma 4, starting tests of whether data-center AI chips can survive heat and radiation in space. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI
item.description: NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 Super, a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts with 12B active, adds a built-in drafter and 4-bit weights, reaching 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro. (NVIDIA, Aastha Jhunjhunwala, Aayushi Ashokkumar Srivastava et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
item.description: Weight normalization's pretraining gains over weight decay come mostly from its effective learning-rate trajectory; scheduling that quantity with a theory-derived inverse-square-root shape (AIR) cuts MoE loss about 0.01 below cosine. (Qifan Yu, Xinyu Ma, Xingyan Bin et al. · ByteDance Seed, Peking University)

item.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
item.description: Exponential residual flows give discrete diffusion language models an analogue of the probability-flow ODE: after one random draw, sampling is deterministic yet provably keeps the right distributions, enabling consistency distillation. (Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Eric Moulines et al. · École polytechnique, MBZUAI, EPITA)

item.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
item.description: Training a chatbot to write an explicit, rule-checkable safety decision before it replies turns the shallowness of safety alignment into a defense against multi-turn jailbreaks, without a judge model in the reward. (Qiyao Ma, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang et al. · Microsoft Research, University of California, Davis)

item.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
item.description: In compute-matched experiments, spending part of a pretraining budget on synthetic pre-pretraining never beats spending it on natural text, and an earlier reported gain disappears once the baseline's initialization is improved. (Alexander Stern, Tim Rocktäschel, Acyr Locatelli et al. · Cohere, UCL AI Centre, MIT)
